svg.title: The Go installer sets up the developer's own shell: Without sudo, the Go installer writes GOROOT and GOPATH to the startup file of zsh, once
svg.text: The Go installer sets up the developer's own shell
Scenario: Without sudo, the Go installer writes GOROOT and GOPATH to the startup file of zsh, once

g.text: Given a developer whose login shell is zsh has no sudo and no Go
A fresh Ubuntu machine where the developer's login shell is zsh: $SHELL is /bin/zsh. The
account has no sudo, so sudo asks for a password, and Go is not installed.
~/.zshrc holds the four lines Ubuntu puts in ~/.profile: ~/.local/bin joins the PATH when
that folder exists. It does not exist yet, so this terminal does not have it.

text.tspan: echo "$SHELL"; sudo -n true; type go; cat ~/.zshrc

g.text: When the Go installer runs without sudo, it adds GOROOT and GOPATH to
The developer runs the Go installer, the same line task dev:setup-environment runs. Without
sudo it installs Go in the home folder, under ~/.local/go, and exits with code 0.
~/.zshrc now ends with the two lines the installer added: GOROOT, where Go lives, and GOPATH,
where go install puts what it builds.
Then a new zsh has GOROOT and GOPATH set and runs Go
A new zsh reads ~/.zshrc: GOROOT and GOPATH are set, ~/.local/bin is now on the PATH, and go
And a second run of the installer does not add the lines twice
Back in the first terminal, Go is still not on the PATH: ~/.local/bin did not exist when it
opened. So a second run installs Go again.
grep finds GOROOT and GOPATH once each, on lines 6 and 7 of ~/.zshrc: the second run did not
